fivetran.name: Fivetran
fivetran.summary: A hosted service billed on monthly active rows per connection, with the full rate card published.
fivetran.bestWhen: you want a hosted service, many ready-made connectors, or database sources such as Oracle.
fivetran.watchOut: each connection has its own curve, small connections carry a $5 base, deletes and history mode now count, and annual contracts start at $12,000 (pay-as-you-go has no minimum).

airbyte.name: Airbyte Cloud
airbyte.summary: Billed in credits: 4 per GB for databases and files, 6 per million rows for APIs.
airbyte.bestWhen: you want a published credit price and a low monthly entry point.
airbyte.watchOut: credits are a different meter from rows, so estimate with your own data before comparing.

hevo.name: Hevo
hevo.summary: Billed on events (each record inserted, updated or deleted), with a free tier.
hevo.bestWhen: a small team wants a free start and a monthly tier it can plan around.
hevo.watchOut: every inserted, updated or deleted record is an event, so busy tables use the allowance fast.

stitch.name: Stitch
stitch.summary: Billed on replicated rows per month, with a Standard plan from $100 a month for 5M rows.
stitch.bestWhen: you want a simple row-based tier at a few million rows.
stitch.watchOut: this guide only covers its entry plan, so check the pricing page for the rest.

estuary.name: Estuary
estuary.summary: Billed on data moved at $0.50 per GB, plus per-connector fees.
estuary.bestWhen: you would rather pay by data volume than by distinct rows.
estuary.watchOut: connector fees sit on top of the per-GB rate, so each source and destination adds to the bill.

selfhost.name: Self-hosted open source
selfhost.summary: Open-source ingestion you run yourself, with no per-row bill.
selfhost.bestWhen: you mostly land production databases in a lake or warehouse and your team can run the software.
selfhost.watchOut: it is not automatically cheaper: compute, storage requests, table maintenance and operator time take the place of the row bill.
